system.name: Terrier Luna imputation of blank consumer-file fields
system.description: Completion of blank sci_* fields: stratified RF/KNN with logistic calibration, the prior-corrected rare-class repair, the household model, the GPU XGBoost round, majority-default and household-copy statuses, and the per-district refits for OR-05 and CT-01.

components.name: Luna stratified RF/KNN completion
components.computes: Per-field calibrated class probabilities for blank sci_* values; most probable class fills the blank.
components.method: StratifiedGroupKFold by household; RF (128 trees) vs KNN grid; logistic calibration; promotion gate on A2. Colorado holdout 86.67-86.76%. Per-district refits: OR-05 86.64% vs 77.89% majority; CT-01 87.39% vs 77.91%.
assumptions: No untouched labels remain in Colorado
empirical_questions: Is missingness in vendor consumer fields MAR given observed fields?
Does a model trained on one district transfer to another?
components.heading: Luna stratified RF-KNN completion

components.name: Prior-corrected rare-class repair
components.computes: Rare-class probability under balanced weights x training prevalence, renormalized.
assumptions: Balanced weights inflate rare classes by about inverse prevalence
empirical_questions: Does prior correction improve calibration of rare classes on holdout?
components.heading: Prior-corrected rare-class repair

components.name: Household model
components.computes: RF with leave-one-out household co-member labels: +1.009 pp holdout (95% +0.959 to +1.060). The shuffled-household control removes the gain.
empirical_questions: How much predictive information do household co-members carry for consumer attributes?
components.heading: Household model

components.name: GPU XGBoost round and fill-status rules
components.computes: XGBoost or RF500 fills in 8 fields (+0.087 pp on second holdout use). Majority-default status when lift < 0.5 pp. Historical household copy.
components.method: Section 30 is current. Bigger models gained only about +0.1 pp, so the ceiling is the information in the data.
assumptions: Lift over majority tests the information content of a field
empirical_questions: Is imputation accuracy capped by data information rather than model capacity?
components.heading: GPU XGBoost round and fill-status rules

evidence.title: Validating the Applicability of Bayesian Inference with Surname and Geocoding to Congressional Redistricting
evidence.claim: Modal assignment gives a longer right tail of precinct error for White voters and higher district error than summed probabilities in nearly all simulated districts. For Black voters, PSM vastly outperforms PM at precinct level.
evidence.system_side: models.py lines 386-393 score Luna candidates by argmax accuracy against a modal majority baseline (confirmed). measures.py lines 197-220 count literal codes with raw.eq(code) over valid-code denominators (confirmed). The step that fills each blank with the most probable class was not located in the lines read. The 78 percent majority baseline was not found in the code.
evidence.transfer: Applies only if modal-filled codes reach an area-level share. Whether the v3 ingest reads the Luna-completed file remains unconfirmed. The rare-class under-count is a hypothesis; the paper measures bias for race only, not for vendor consumer fields.
